extracted.intended_audience: applicants preparing NIH grant application attachments (PIs, research administrators, grants staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, formatting, and submitting PDF attachments for NIH grant applications so they meet system requirements and reviewer expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF format requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachments must be prepared outside the grant application using any editing software and converted to PDF format; we require PDF format to preserve document formatting and a consistent reading experience for reviewers and staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to follow these requirements may lead to application errors upon submission or withdrawal from funding consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character set (Unicode)
rubrics_metrics.description: eRA systems support the Unicode character set (including Greek and other special characters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NOT-OD-15-058. Tip: use preview features in ASSIST and verify information in eRA Commons after submission, especially when non-standard characters are used; contact eRA Service Desk with questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations — format and public access
rubrics_metrics.description: Use whatever format for citations you want; NIH does not require a specific citation format and 'et al.' is acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include PMC reference number (PMCID) when citing applicable papers per public access policy. SciENcv uses the 'Citing Medicine' format and may be useful if your organization has no standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining information into a single attachment
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure all information is directly visible in your PDF. If combining information from different sources, do not use 'bundling' or 'portfolio' features that provide links to individual files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine into a single document prior to uploading so content is directly visible; avoid linked documents that hide content behind links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic signatures policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic signatures on PDF attachments within your application are not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To adhere to policies requiring electronic signatures on attachments, you can electronically sign the document and then 'flatten' the PDF; alternatively print, sign, scan and attach the signed PDF. Flattening merges layers so eRA can process the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filenames — length, uniqueness, allowed characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Save all document attachments with descriptive filenames of 50 characters or less (including spaces). Use unique filenames for all attachments in an application (or within a component of a multi-project application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed characters: A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscore, hyphen, space, period, parenthesis, curly braces, square brackets, tilde, exclamation point, comma, apostrophe, at sign, number sign, dollar sign, percent sign, plus sign, and equal sign. If including spaces, use one space (not two or more). Do not begin the filename with a space or include a space immediately before the .pdf extension. Avoid ampersand (&) since it requires special formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: File size limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure file size is greater than 0 bytes - we cannot accept a 0 byte attachment. Keep attachment file size to 100 MB or less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce image/file size (e.g., using JPEG or PNG compression) to stay within limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flattened PDFs required
rubrics_metrics.description: PDFs included in applications, progress reports, and other information collected in eRA Commons must be flattened so all layers are merged into a single flat layer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PDFs with fillable fields, electronic signatures, text boxes, or images may become layered and must be flattened. Uploading an unflattened PDF may result in an eRA Commons error message and require replacement with a flattened version. Easiest method: print as PDF; follow eRA illustrated instructions for Windows and Mac.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font size minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: Text in attachments must be 11 points or larger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smaller text in graphics, figures, graphs, diagrams, and charts is acceptable if legible at 100% view. Some PDF conversion software reduces font size—confirm final PDF compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type density limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Type density must be no more than 15 characters per linear inch (including characters and spaces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is to ensure readability and fairness; attachments with greater density may be withdrawn from consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line spacing limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Line spacing must be no more than six lines per vertical inch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text color guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no restriction on text color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Black or other high-contrast colors are recommended as they print well and are legible to the largest audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended fonts
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH recommends fonts such as Arial, Georgia, Helvetica, Palatino Linotype, but other serif and non-serif fonts are acceptable if they meet minimum requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legibility is paramount; failure to conform to minimum font/type/spacing requirements may result in withdrawal from consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format pages (use required format pages where specified)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some attachment instructions refer to required format pages (e.g., biosketch, other support, training data tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the format pages referenced in specific funding opportunity instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headers and footers — do not include
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include headers or footers in your attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH adds headers, footers, page numbers, bookmarks, and a table of contents when assembling your grant application upon submission. Headings within the text (e.g., Significance, Innovation) are encouraged to improve readability. Some FOAs require specific headings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperlinks and URLs policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyperlinks and URLs are only allowed when specifically noted in funding opportunities and/or form field instructions; hyperlinks and URLs may not be used to provide information necessary to application review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must be self-contained; reviewers are not obligated to view linked sites and are cautioned about accessing external sites. When allowed, you must display the actual URL text on the page (do not hide behind hypertext). See NOT-OD-20-174 and Hyperlinks within Common Forms FAQs. Note: temporary leniency for hypertext in the DMS Plan during initial policy implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures — readability and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Images and other figures must be readable as printed on an 8.5” x 11” page at normal (100%) scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include figures in the Research Strategy, Program Plan, or equivalent attachment; they count towards page limits and should not be included in the Specific Aims attachment. Project Summary/Abstract and Project Narrative attachments should only include text (no figures) unless otherwise stated. Use image compression to reduce file size and consider accessibility elements like structural headers and meaningful Alt Text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and style — English and acronyms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use English. Avoid jargon. Spell out acronyms the first time they are used in each application section or attachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note the appropriate abbreviation in parentheses; the abbreviation may be used thereafter in that section or attachment. Refer to NIH Grants Policy Statement abbreviations list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not markup attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not markup your PDF documents with comments, sticky notes, or other features that are added on top of your PDF document content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information may not be retained in your final application image. Do not use bracketing, indenting, highlighting, bolding, italicizing, underlining, margin lines, change in typography, font, or font color, or any other markup to identify changes in Resubmission Applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation — portrait preferred for readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Both portrait and landscape attachments are accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Landscape can be difficult to read online and may require reviewers and staff to scroll to see all text; choose portrait for easier online review where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits and lines-of-text limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to the page limits defined in the Table of Page Limits or within the funding opportunity or NIH Guide notice. If no page limit is listed you can assume the attachment does not have a limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page limits are strictly enforced and include all text on the page including headers. Lines-of-text limits are not systematically enforced. Some page limits apply to multiple attachments combined — prepare accordingly. NIH systems provide error/warning messages but do not replace manual staff checks. Do not use appendices or other sections to circumvent page limits (see NOT-OD-11-080).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper size and margins
rubrics_metrics.description: Use paper no larger than standard letter paper size (8 ½" x 11"). Provide at least one-half inch (½") margins — top, bottom, left, and right — for all pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No applicant-supplied information can appear in the margins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid scanning text documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid scanning text documents to produce the required PDFs; it is best to produce documents using word processing software and convert to PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scanning may hamper automated processing; recognize sometimes scanning is necessary for signed documents or letters on letterhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disable PDF security features
rubrics_metrics.description: Disable all security features in your PDF documents. Do not encrypt or password protect your documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security features prevent NIH systems from opening and processing attached documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-column page format encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: A single-column page format easily adapts to various screen sizes and is highly encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multi-column formats, especially for multi-page content, can be problematic for online review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video materials — restricted post-submission use
rubrics_metrics.description: Videos cannot be embedded in an application, but videos are accepted under limited circumstances as post-submission material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When allowed, the cover letter must state intent to submit a video; otherwise it will not be accepted. Key images ('stills') and a brief description of each video must be included within the page limits of the Research Strategy so reviewers can understand the content if they cannot access the video.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preview and verification recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use preview features in ASSIST and other systems prior to submission and verify information in eRA Commons after submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is especially important when non-standard characters are used. Contact the eRA Service Desk with any questions or concerns.
